qt: to the Commission Galato Alexandraki (ECR) Subject:

On 8 July 2026, the Commission sent a reasoned opinion to Greece for failing to fully transpose Directive (EU) 2023/2668 on the protection of workers from exposure to asbestos. The deadline for implementing most of the provisions expired on 21 December 2025. The directive reduces the permissible exposure limit from 0.1 to 0.01 fibres per cubic centimetre. The delay is especially serious for those working on demolition and renovation sites and in old public buildings, where the presence of asbestos could endanger their health. In view of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.
What provisions has Greece not yet transposed and what is its timetable for compliance?
How is the implementation of the new exposure limit in Greek workplaces currently being monitored?
Does it intend to require specific checks to be carried out on EU-funded renovation and energy retrofit projects?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (12.11.2026) The reasoned opinion that the Commission sent to Greece for failing to notify measures for the transposition into national law of Directive (EU) 2023/2668 on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work1 concerns the provisions of the Directive which the Member States had to transpose by 21 December 2025 according to Article 2(1) and (2) of the Directive. In the reasoned opinion, the Commission invited Greece to take the necessary measures to comply with the obligation to adopt and notify transposition measures within two months of receipt of the reasoned opinion. The Commission is assessing the responses received from the Member States to which a reasoned opinion was addressed, including Greece. Member States must transpose EU directives into national legislation. Competent national authorities are primarily responsible for monitoring the implementation and for enforcing national provisions transposing EU directives. They are also responsible for dealing with issues related to compliance with EU law in concrete individual cases. Under Cohesion policy, EU-funded renovation and energy retrofit projects must comply with applicable EU and national law. In line with shared management principles, managing authorities are responsible for verifying that co-financed operations comply with applicable law. The implementation of any projects involving activities in which workers are or may be exposed in the course of their work to dust arising from asbestos or materials containing asbestos must adhere to the rules on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work.
1 Directive (EU) 2023/2668 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 22 November 2023 amending
Directive 2009/148/EC on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX%3A32023L2668&qid=1789968446827.
